findings.evidence: "Real 70B-class dense models commonly use grouped-query attention (GQA): LLaMA-2 70B, for instance, has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads, so per-token KV shrinks by the head ratio to KVGQA per-token = 2 × nlayers × nKV-heads × dhead × B = 2 × 80 × (8 × 128) × 2 B ≈0.33 MB/token — about 8× smaller."
findings.issue: LLaMA-2 70B uses standard multi-head attention with 64 key/value heads (num_key_value_heads=64 = num_attention_heads), not GQA with 8 KV-heads. GQA was introduced after Llama 2's release and first used in Llama 3. The model with 8 KV-heads and the stated 0.33 MB/token arithmetic is LLaMA-3 70B, not LLaMA-2 70B. As stated, the text attributes a ~8× KV reduction to a model that would actually hold the full-MHA ~2.62 MB/token, undermining the sensitivity note's purpose of showing readers how GQA changes the KV constant.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace "LLaMA-2 70B" with "LLaMA-3 70B" in the attention-family sensitivity note in Ch. 7 §3. Also verify that every other instance of a "Llama-2" + GQA pairing is corrected or removed (see R18-002).

findings.page: PDF p. 172 (printed p. 148) and PDF p. 177 (printed p. 153); policy at PDF p. 21 (printed p. xvii) and comparator at PDF p. 171 (printed p. 147)
findings.chapter: Ch. 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint (§7.3.2, §7.3.3)
findings.evidence: §7.3.2 (PDF p. 172): "Its language configuration has 16 full-attention layers, four KV-heads per layer, and a head dimension of 256 (released configuration, retrieved 2026-10-28)." and "[1P][FACT] for the configuration, including that 262,144-token maximum context length". §7.3.3 (PDF p. 177): "[1P][FACT] for the GGUF specification content (GGUF specification, pinned revision, retrieved 2026-10-28)". By contrast the immediately preceding subsection (§7.3.1, PDF p. 171) names the revision: "These datasheets were admitted under post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff, as dated device-capacity documentation". The Preface (PDF p. 21) states the rule: "the separately dated 2026-10-28 technology notes in the body and Appendix A carry revision v20260913+addendum-20261028". Ch. 5's footnotes (PDF pp. 127, 139) use the partial form "retrieved 2026-10-28 (post-cutoff addendum: outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff...)" with no revision identifier.
findings.issue: Two body subsections import post-cutoff evidence (retrieved 2026-10-28) and label it [1P][FACT] without carrying the addendum revision the Preface mandates for dated 2026-10-28 technology notes, while the sibling subsection one page earlier and the comparable Ch. 2/Ch. 3 passages do carry 'v20260913+addendum-20261028'. The Ch. 5 footnotes use a third, unnumbered form ('post-cutoff addendum:') that also fails to name the revision. Since the book's edition rule ties a revision identifier to each dated post-cutoff claim so a reader can tell which claims sit outside the 2026-08-30 snapshot, the unnamed revisions in §7.3.2/§7.3.3 break that traceability for the two claims the book treats as first-party facts (the Qwen3.8-27B attention configuration and the GGUF specification content).
findings.fix_instruction: Add the revision identifier to every body note dated 2026-10-28: e.g. in §7.3.2 change '(released configuration, retrieved 2026-10-28)' to '(released configuration, retrieved 2026-10-28 — post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff)', and in §7.3.3 do the same for the GGUF specification citation. Apply the same fix to the two Ch. 5 footnotes so that 'post-cutoff addendum:' is replaced by the explicit 'v20260913+addendum-20261028'.
